public_rationale: Marcus explicitly said there was “almost zero chance” of AGI arriving within two to three years. That is a probability assessment. The supplied reviewer instruction excludes such claims from scoring. Treating AGI's arrival as automatic contradiction, or its nonarrival as automatic support, would replace his statement with a categorical forecast. The stated window ends March 5, 2028, after the evaluation date, but the reason for this disposition is the probability exclusion.
limitations: This disposition does not assess whether Marcus's probability estimate was reasonable.
It makes no finding about whether any system meets the quoted AGI definition.

our_interpretation: Marcus assigns a very low probability to AGI arriving within the stated period. He does not assert that its arrival is impossible.
The latest endpoint of the stated window is March 5, 2028, three years after publication.
The GPT 4.5 remark supplies a reason for his probability assessment, not a condition that must occur before the forecast applies.
The supplied reviewer instruction excludes probability claims from scoring. Recasting this statement as a categorical prediction of no AGI would change what Marcus said.
criteria.support_condition: No admissible binary outcome test under the supplied exclusion of probability claims. Nonarrival within the window would not establish that the probability was almost zero when Marcus spoke.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No admissible binary outcome test under the supplied exclusion of probability claims. Arrival within the window would not by itself establish that Marcus's stated probability was wrong when assigned.
